title: Pi dependency, worker protocol, and workspace tools
objective: Pin Pi and define the narrow, versioned, secret-free protocol and custom tools that let a child runtime work throughout its disposable SCORE workspace without reaching the host project.
requirements: The project pins @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent exactly at 0.84.1, raises the Node engine floor to 22.19.0, and records a deterministic lockfile update.

A versioned JSON-lines worker protocol carries one frozen Job request and bounded lifecycle facts without serializing credentials, raw prompts, transcripts, model output, or arbitrary environment variables.

The Pi worker receives only SCORE-owned list, read, write, and delete tools that accept canonical workspace-relative paths, resolve them beneath the supplied disposable workspace, and reject absolute paths, traversal, and symlink escape.

Workspace tools permit reading and disposable mutation of the target, context, and scratch paths inside the workspace, enforce UTF-8, size, and safe-file-type rules, and never access host paths outside the workspace root.

Deterministic tests validate protocol decoding, unknown-version rejection, secret-free serialization, tool schemas, internal context and scratch mutations, workspace confinement, and unsafe filesystem cases.

skills.name: Closed JSON-lines IPC
skills.content: Use Effect Schema to define a closed versioned request and tagged event union. Encode canonical JSON plus one newline. Decode one line only and fail closed on unknown keys, tags, versions, invalid JSON, or oversized lines. Requests may carry only isolated file paths, identifiers, the closed Agent Input JSON, and pinned versions; events may carry only stable lifecycle facts and sanitized bounded messages.

constraints: Do not include API keys, OAuth tokens, environment maps, prompts beyond Agent Input JSON, transcripts, assistant content, tool arguments, or tool output in any schema.
Cap every accepted line and diagnostic message before parsing or persistence.
Do not import the Pi SDK in this module.
Do not change another file.

context.purpose: Defines the outer disposable workspace confinement and target-only candidate extraction these tools must complement.
Documents why Pi built-in filesystem and bash tools are not cwd-confined and must not be exposed.

skills.name: Capability-shaped Pi tools
skills.content: Use Pi's custom tool definition API to create only list, read, write, and delete operations over canonical workspace-relative paths. Resolve and validate every request beneath the one canonical workspace root; reject absolute paths, `..`, empty or ambiguous segments, symlinks, sockets, devices, and any canonical escape. Permit context edits, context deletion, nested creates, and scratch files inside the workspace because only the assigned target is later collected. Enforce bounded UTF-8 content and return bounded metadata, never content echoes.

constraints: Do not expose Pi's built-in read, write, edit, bash, grep, find, or ls tools because their paths are not workspace-confined.
Tool schemas may accept only canonical workspace-relative paths and UTF-8 content; they may not accept cwd, command, glob, URL, or environment fields.
Use Effect-wrapped filesystem calls with explicit root, parent, and lstat checks; never follow symlinks.
Do not change another file.
